Filtronic
UK  |  Satellite Ground Systems
Contract Win
Filtronic has been awarded UK Space Agency funding to develop a new RF-over-IP demonstrator, letting ground stations move radio signals over standard Ethernet instead of complex analog wiring — supporting up to 100Gb/s across X, Ka and V-band satellite links. As operators shift to software-defined, cloud-native networks, it's exactly the kind of infrastructure that keeps UK ground segment expertise ahead of the curve.
🔗 Source: Filtronic
👤 LinkedIn Post
Big signal from the UK's satellite ground segment sector this week. Filtronic has been awarded UK Space Agency funding to develop a new RF-over-IP demonstrator — technology that lets ground stations transport radio signals over standard Ethernet instead of complex analog wiring, supporting up to 100Gb/s across X, Ka and V-band. As satellite operators move to software-defined, cloud-native networks, this is exactly the kind of infrastructure that keeps UK ground segment expertise ahead of the curve. Proud to have Filtronic exhibiting at Space-Comm Expo Europe 2027. GMV
Spain  |  Mission Operations / Ground Segment
ESA Contract
GMV has been named prime contractor for Phase 1 of Pulse, ESA's next-generation mission control system built on the EGS-CC framework — covering the Swarm mission migration and prepping Euclid for validation testing. A strong vote of confidence in GMV's ground segment engineering as ESA standardises how it runs missions.
🔗 Source: GMV
👤 LinkedIn Post
ESA just handed GMV the keys to its next-generation mission control system. GMV has been named prime contractor for Phase 1 of Pulse, built on ESA's EGS-CC framework — the reusable mission control platform set to run operations across ESA's satellite portfolio, starting with migrating the Swarm mission and prepping Euclid for validation testing. It's a vote of confidence in GMV's ground segment engineering at exactly the moment ESA is standardising how it runs missions. Proud to have GMV exhibiting at Space-Comm Expo Europe 2027. European Space Sovereignty Push
Germany / EU  |  Government / Defence
Industry News
Germany has committed €35 billion to sovereign military space capability by 2030, part of a wider European push for independent ISR and satellite capacity — forecast to grow more than fourfold by 2035 — after US restrictions on satellite data access during recent crises. Germany has already ordered a 40-satellite constellation from Finland's ICEYE, with France, Poland, Bulgaria, Sweden and the Netherlands moving in the same direction.
🔗 Source: Defense News
👤 LinkedIn Post
Germany just committed €35 billion to sovereign military space capability by 2030. It's part of a much bigger European shift: after US restrictions on satellite data access during recent crises, European nations are racing to build independent ISR and satellite capacity — expected to grow more than fourfold by 2035. Germany's already ordered a 40-satellite constellation from Finland's ICEYE, and France, Poland, Bulgaria, Sweden and the Netherlands are all moving in the same direction. This is exactly the kind of procurement shift commercial space companies need to be in the room for — which is exactly what Space-Comm Expo Europe exists to deliver. ESA Commercial Cargo Contract
Europe  |  Government / Procurement
Industry News
ESA has awarded The Exploration Company a €760 million contract for up to three Nyx cargo spacecraft flights to the ISS — €310m for a demonstration mission targeting 2028 docking, plus €450m in options for two more. A clear signal that European human spaceflight procurement is shifting toward commercial partnership, with a December ministerial meeting in Rome to decide whether that momentum continues into crewed spaceflight.
🔗 Source: Tech Times
👤 LinkedIn Post
ESA just put €760 million behind a commercial company to fly cargo to the ISS. The Exploration Company has been awarded a contract for up to three Nyx cargo spacecraft flights — €310m for a demonstration mission targeting ISS docking in 2028, plus €450m in options for two more. It's a real signal of where European human spaceflight procurement is heading: less in-house, more commercial partnership. A December ministerial meeting in Rome will decide whether that momentum continues into crewed spaceflight. This is exactly the kind of procurement moment commercial space companies need to be in the room for — which is exactly what Space-Comm Expo Europe exists to deliver.
